newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Cardoso sees more Mercosur accords soon.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Cardoso sees more Mercosur accords soon.

text.p: Brazil's President Fernando Henrique Cardoso, praising the successes of the four-nation Mercosur customs union, said Tuesday he foresees accords between the union and the rest of South America soon.

In his weekly radio address, Cardoso said Mercosur partners Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay will sign agreements on consumer protection, defense, education, the environment and trade when they meet next Tuesday in northeastern Brazil.
He said that, in the near future, Mercosur would extend those accords to include the remaining countries in the region. But he did not provide a date by when that might happen.
"In little time, we intend to extend (those agreements) to the other countries in South America," Cardoso said.
Cardoso and his Mercosur counterparts are slated to sign a free-trade accord with Bolivia when they meet next week in the city of Fortaleza.
The pact would grant the Andean nation associate status in Mercosur, akin to that granted to Chile earlier this year.
